prompt:
Image 1 is a finished game sprite sheet whose drawing is right: keep exactly its camera (high above and in front, looking down at about 40 degrees), the direction every figure faces, every figure's pose, size and position in its cell, the 4 by 4 grid and the flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background. Image 1 shows a levy spearman of another army whose cloth was already dyed green for this sheet.
Image 2 is a painted portrait from the same game, a reference for the painting hand and the materials only: do not paint that person, and do not copy its dark background, its candlelight or its framing.

A previous attempt at this sheet failed: a pink cast was left on the spear head and the edge of the face in the follow-through cell. Keep every edge in the figure's own colours: bone, iron, wood and skin, never pink.

Repaint every figure of Image 1 as a different soldier, the same soldier in every cell. Keep each figure's pose, the position of its arms, legs and weapon, and its outline as close as the new kit allows. His iron skullcap and cloth band become a deep bottle-green hood, worn up; his short hooded shoulder cape becomes a short deep bottle-green hooded cloak over his shoulders and upper back; his padded jack becomes a bark-brown leather jerkin with padded sleeves and leather bracers; the long surcoat stays, deep bottle green, to just below the knees, held by a knotted rope belt; his face is bark-brown and weathered; the spear becomes a long dark hawthorn spear with a barbed head of bone and iron shaped like a great thorn, held exactly where the spear is held. Every figure keeps the outline of Image 1: the same silhouette, the same arms, legs and weapon in the same places, the same size and the same place in its cell; only the clothes, armour, skin and the weapon's own shape change. Do not re-pose any figure, even where its pose looks unusual for this soldier.

The soldier: A Thorn Militia levy spearman: a bark-brown leather jerkin, worn under a sleeveless surcoat of deep bottle-green cloth that covers his whole chest and belly from the collar down to just below the knees, front and back, split at the front below the belt so the legs can stride and held at the waist by a knotted rope belt; a short deep bottle-green hooded cloak with the hood up, covering the shoulders and the upper back; padded sleeves and leather bracers; wrapped legs and soft boots; bark-brown weathered skin; a long dark hawthorn spear with a barbed head of bone and iron shaped like a great thorn. No shield, no antlers. Plain and poor.

Side colour: the raised hood, the short cloak and the long surcoat are cloth dyed deep bottle green: the colour of jade or of a green glass bottle held to the light, a clear and fairly saturated cool green; never leaf-green, olive, grey or blackish, never as blue as teal. These are large, clean, unbroken areas that face the sky and the camera, so that a packed block of these soldiers reads as that colour from far away.

Paint him in the hand of the game's painted portraits: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, a muted earthy palette, small crisp highlights on metal edges and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges; nothing glows unless the description says so. Keep the daylight of Image 1 (a high sun from the upper left, a cool fill on the lower right). Realistic adult proportions; no cartoon, no thick outlines.

Facing, again: every figure faces exactly as in Image 1, toward us and to the lower left, the hit and the falling figures included; the fleeing figures run as in Image 1.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor or shadow. No magenta, pink or purple anywhere on the figures. Never: text, labels, grid lines, borders, a floor, cast shadows, blood, extra people, cropped or overlapping figures.
